method: Each product is a whole-number combination m1f1 + m2f2 (plus m3f3 when a third carrier is entered), and its order is the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients, so 2f1 - f2 is third order and 3f1 - 2f2 is fifth. Every coefficient triple from minus the chosen order to plus the chosen order is enumerated, kept when that absolute sum lies between two and the chosen order and the resulting frequency is positive, and rounded to six decimal places in MHz. Products that share a frequency are listed once, keeping the lowest order that produces them, because lower orders are normally the stronger products; the list is then sorted by frequency. Single-carrier harmonics such as 2f1 and 3f2 are included. A protect band, given as a low and a high limit, marks each product whose frequency falls on or inside those limits. Frequencies must be greater than zero and at most 1,000,000 MHz, orders run from 2 to 7, and the protect band requires both limits with the low one below the high one. The model is frequency arithmetic only: it does not consider transmit levels, mixer intercept points, receiver selectivity, antenna coupling, spectral masks or the applicable band plan, so it is not an interference or authorisation determination. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Two-tone intermodulation products: m1f1 + m2f2 with the order defined as |m1| + |m2|
Third-order products such as 2f1 - f2 and 2f2 - f1 fall closest to the carriers and are usually the strongest mixing products
Coincident product frequencies are listed once at the lowest order that produces them
